deficits.evidence: The footway is an informal path without a purpose-built sidewalk.
deficits.suggestion: Construct a purpose-built sidewalk on the left side of the road to provide a safe walking space.

deficits.evidence: The informal path is uneven and broken.
deficits.suggestion: Level and pave the informal path on the left to remove trip hazards.

deficits.evidence: The sidewalk is uneven and broken in several places.
deficits.suggestion: Repair the broken sections of the sidewalk on the right side.

deficits.evidence: There is high crossing demand due to the urban environment and buildings, but no designated crossing facility is provided.
deficits.suggestion: Install a marked pedestrian crossing to allow people to cross the road safely.

ratings.reason: The left side lacks a formal sidewalk, and building one is feasible and specific to this location.
The unpaved area on the left is clearly uneven, and repairing it is a feasible, specific fix.
The right-side footway shows visible deterioration and debris, making repair a feasible and specific improvement.
The urban setting shows high activity but no marked crossings, and installing one is a standard, feasible street design change.
